name: GATE Overflow CS Test Series 2025 | Mock GATE | Test 4

question.text:
Fill in the blanks with the right words:
The ________ judgment caused ________ in the courthouse.

  1. forgiving, heated
  2. lenient, scoff
  3. heavy, brawl
  4. controversial, disarray

A dishonest dealer pretends to sell at the cost price but earns a profit of $53\%$ by under weighing. What weight must he be using for $1$ kg?

  1. $653.549$ gm
  2. $653.594$ gm
  3. $653.593$ gm
  4. $653.597$ gm

Every year, a survey of $10000$ people is conducted by the World Health Organization (WHO). WHO found that in the years $2016, 2017, 2018, 2019$ and $2020$ the percentage of people affected by  typhoid were $40\%, 50\%, 45\%, 25\%$ and $20\%$ respectively. WHO also found that every year out of the affected people $50\%$ were students, $20\%$ were house-wives and $30\%$ were drivers. The number of house-wives, students and drivers were in the ratio $25 : 13 : 12,$ every year.

If $\alpha$ is the year having the minimum number of students not affected by typhoid, the number of students not affected by typhoid among the sample of $10000$ in year $\alpha$ is _________

Helioseismology is to Sun what Epidemiology is to ________

  1. Earth
  2. Medicine
  3. Moon
  4. Disease

Two capitalized words which have a certain relationship to each other are given below, followed by four pairs of words. Choose the pair that is related to each other in the same way as the given pair of words.
$\textbf{SIMMER : BOIL}$

  1. Ice : Water
  2. Hot : Cold
  3. Chill : Freeze
  4. Roast : Fry

If the square of the $4^{\text{th}}$ term of an arithmetic progression with common difference $(>1)$ equals the product of the $5^{\text{th}}$ and $13^{\text{th}}$ terms, then the ratio of the $40^{\text{th}}$ term to the $79^{\text{th}}$ term is ?

  1. $9:19$
  2. $1:2$
  3. $19:9$
  4. $2:1$

The funnel chart given below shows percentage distribution of five different age groups of a
particular city.
 

If the total population increases at rate of $5\%$ per annum and the current total population is $1$ lakh, what will be the population of age group of $5 \leq x < 20$ after $2$ years? [if percentage distribution remains the same]

The solution for the inequality $5x-7 < 2x < 13x-31$ is

  1. $\left(-\infty, -\dfrac{7}{3}\right)$
  2. $\left(\dfrac{31}{3},\infty \right)$
  3. $\left(-\infty, -\dfrac{31}{11}\right)$
  4. No solution

A person's present age is one-seventh of the age of his mother. After $6$ years, he will be one-fourth of the age of his mother. How old is the mother at present?

  1. $35$
  2. $28$
  3. $49$
  4. $42$

A person invested $Rs.\,5041$ by dividing into $3$ parts. The rate of interest per annum for the first, second and third parts are $2\%,7\%\,\text{and}\, 4\%$ respectively. At the end of the year, he got the same simple interest in all three parts. What is the amount of money (rounded to the nearest integer) he invested at $7\%?$

  1. $Rs.\; 994$
  2. $Rs.\; 807$
  3. $Rs.\; 894$
  4. $Rs.\; 934$

Consider the following synchronization solution for Producer-Consumer problem. Here, counter is a shared variable initialized to 0, buffer is the shared memory region and increment and decrement operations take place atomically.

Consumer process
item nextConsumed;
while (1) {
    while (counter == 0);
    nextConsumed = buffer[out];
    out = (out + 1) % BUFFER_SIZE;
    counter--;
}
Producer process
item nextProduced;
while (1) {
    while (counter == BUFFER_SIZE);
    buffer[in] = nextProduced;
    in = (in + 1) % BUFFER_SIZE;
    counter++;
}


Which of the following is correct?

  1. Race condition may be possible.
  2. The solution works fine for Producer Consumer problem.
  3. Progress is violating.
  4. Buffer overflow is possible.

How many different ways can eight identical cookies be distributed among three distinct children if each child receives at least two cookies and no more than four cookies?
  1. $7$
  2. $6$
  3. $8$
  4. $9$

Let $G$ be an undirected connected graph with distinct edge weights. Let $e_{\text{max}}$ and $e_{\text{min}}$ be the edges with maximum and minimum edge weights. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE? (Mark all the appropriate choices)

  1. If $e_{\text{min}}$ is present in some cycle then every Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of $G$ must include $e_{\text{min}}$.
  2. $e_{\text{max}}$ will must be absent in every MST.
  3. $G$ will have a unique MST if $e_{\text{max}}$ is present in MST.
  4. MST of $G$ will never contain $e_{\text{min}}$ and $e_{\text{max}}$ at the same time.

What is the minimum number of color required to color this graph?
 

  1. $4$
  2. $3$
  3. $2$
  4. $5$

Which one of the following is/are correct? (Mark all the appropriate choices)

  1. Compulsory misses can be reduced by increasing the total cache size.
  2. Capacity misses can be reduced by increasing the block size.
  3. Conflict misses may be reduced by increasing the value of associativity.
  4. Compulsory misses can be reduced by increasing the cache block size.

Which of the following is/are regular grammar for the given finite automata? (Mark all the appropriate choices)

  1. $S_{1} \rightarrow aS_{2} \\
    S_{2} \rightarrow a S_{2} \mid bS_{2}$
  2. $S_{1} \rightarrow aS_{2} \\
    S_{2} \rightarrow a S_{2} \mid bS_{2} \mid \varepsilon$
  3. $S_{1} \rightarrow S_{2} a \\
    S_{2} \rightarrow S_{2} a \mid S_{2} b \mid \varepsilon$
  4. $S_{1} \rightarrow S_{1} a \mid S_{1} b \mid S_{2} a \\
    S_{2} \rightarrow \varepsilon$

Consider a Poset on set $A=\{a_1,a_2,\ldots, a_n,x,y\}$ such that

  • $x\leq a_i$ for $i = 1,2,3,4,\dots, n $
  • $a_i \leq y$ for $i = 1,2,3,4,\dots, n $

For any given values of $x$ and $y,$ the number of ways in which the given partial order can be converted to a Totally Ordered Set is ________

  1. $n!$
  2. $(n+1)!$
  3. $n$
  4. $1$

Consider the following page reference string:
$$7, 2, 3, 1, 2, 5, 3, 4, 6, 7,7,1$$
Assume demand paging with three frames, and all frames being initially empty, so the first unique page access cause a page fault.
If $\alpha$ is the number of page faults in optimal page replacement and $\beta$ is the number of page faults in LRU page replacement, the value of $\alpha - \beta$ is _________

Consider an instruction pipeline with five stages without any branch prediction:
Fetch Instruction(FI), Decode Instruction(DI), Fetch Operand(FO), Execute instruction(EI) and Write Operand(WO). The stage delays for FI, DI, FO, EI and WO are $4\;\text{ns}, 5\;\text{ns}, 11\;\text{ns}, 7\;\text{ns}$, and $6\;\text{ns}$ respectively. There are intermediate storage buffers after each stage and the delay of each buffer is $2\;\text{ns}.$ A program consisting of $12$ instructions $I_1, I_2, \ldots I_{12}$ is executed in this pipelined processor. Instruction $I_4$ is the only branch instruction and its branch target is $I_{10}$. If the branch is taken during the execution of this program, the time (in ns) needed to complete the program is _______
The minimum numbers of relations required when the below ER diagram is converted to Relational model ensuring no redundancies is ________

How many $10$ digit numbers have no two digits the same?
  1. $9*9!$
  2. $10!$
  3. $8*9!$
  4. None of these
The coefficient of $x^4$ in the expansion of $(1+x+x^2+x^3+\dots)^3$ is __________

Which of the following is/are true of the UNIX Socket API? (Mark all the appropriate choices)
  1. If a chunk of data written to a TCP socket is smaller than the Maximum Segment Size (MSS), it will all be sent in the same packet.
  2. Writing a single message to a UDP socket can result in the network stack sending multiple packets.
  3. The socket allocated by the accept() system call is assigned a new port number.
  4. We can call connect() on a UDP socket.

Mark all the correct statements given below. $P$ is $l\times m$ and $Q$ is $m \times n$ matrices. (Mark all the appropriate choices)
  1. rank$(P \times P^T) =$ rank$(P)$
  2. rank$(P \times Q) \leq $ rank$(P)$
  3. rank$(P) \leq \min (l,m)$
  4. rank$(0_{n \times n}) = 1$

The minimum value of the function $$f(x) = \frac{x^4}{4} - x^2 -3$$ occurs at
  1. $x = 1$
  2. $x =\sqrt 2$
  3. $x = 0$
  4. $ x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{4}}$

An undirected graph $G(V,E)$ contains $n(n>2)$ nodes named as $1,2,3,4, \dots , n$. Two vertices are adjacent if $0 < \mid i-j \mid \leq 2.$ All the edge weights is unity. How many MST are possible for $n=4$?

A disk has $6$ equidistant tracks. The diameters of the innermost and outermost tracks are $1\;\text{cm}$ and $5\;\text{ cm}$ respectively. The innermost track has a storage capacity of $20\;\text{MB.}$
If the disk has $25$ sectors per track and is currently at the end of the $3^{rd}$ sector of the inner-most track and the head can move at a speed of $10\;\text{meters/sec}$ and it is rotating at constant linear velocity of $7200\;\text{RPM,}$ the time (in milliseconds) it will take to read $16\;\text{MB}$ contiguous data starting from the sector $2$ of the outer-most track will be _________ (rounded to $2$ decimal places)

What is the value returned by the below function when invoked as $fun(20,1)?$

int fun(int x,int y)
{
    if(x/2==0)
        return 0;
    else if(x%2)
        return fun(x/2,3*y) + x + y;
    else
        return fun(x/2,2*y) + x + y;
}
  1. $48$
  2. $49$
  3. $54$
  4. $56$

What is the output of the following program when run on a $64$ bit environment?

#include<stdio.h>
#include<string.h>
int main()
{
    char *a= "GATE 2021";
    char b[ ]="GATE 2021";
    printf("%d %d %d %d %d",
       strlen(a),strlen(b),sizeof(*a),
       sizeof(a),sizeof(b));
}
  1. $9 \: \: 9 \: \: 9 \: \: 1 \: \: 10$
  2. $9 \: \: 9 \: \: 1 \: \: 2 \: \: 12$
  3. $9\:\: 9\:\: 1\:\: 8\:\: 10$
  4. Possible runtime error

Consider a network with five nodes, $N_1$ to $N_5$, as shown as below.


The network uses a Distance Vector Routing protocol. Once the routes have been stabilized, the distance vectors at different nodes are as follows.
$N_{1}: (0, 3, 11, 14, 8)$
$N_{2}: (3, 0, 8, 11, 5)$
$N_{3}: (11, 8, 0, 4, 10)$
$N_{4}: (14, 11, 4, 0, 6)$
$N_{5}: (8, 5, 10, 6, 0)$
Each distance vector is the distance of the best known path at that instance to nodes, $N_{1}$ to $N_{5}$, where the distance to itself is $0$. Also, all links are symmetric and the cost is identical in both directions. In each round, all nodes exchange their distance vectors with their respective neighbors. Then all nodes update their distance vectors. In between two rounds, any change in cost of a link will cause the two incident nodes to change only that entry in their distance vectors.
The cost of link $N_{5}-N_{2}$ reduces to $4$ (in both directions). After the next round of updates, the link $N_{1}-N_{2}$ goes down. $N_{2}$ will reflect this change immediately in its distance vector as cost, $\infty$. After the next round of update, the cost to $N_{1}$ in the distance vector of $N_{5}$ is _______

A certain family has $6$ children, consisting of $3$ boys and $3$ girls. Assuming that all birth orders are equally likely with no twins, what is the probability that the $2$ eldest children are girls? (Up to $2$ decimal places)

Consider a $4$-way set associative cache of size $\text{16 KB}$ and block size $64$ bytes and using $LRU$ replacement. Initially the cache is empty. The following sequence of access to memory blocks:
$${0,64,0,256,300,32,16,257,274,24,19,12}$$
is repeated $10$ times. If the number of conflict misses and compulsory misses are $A$ and $B$ respectively, $2A + 3B =$ _______

An IP router with a Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU) of $1400$ bytes bytes has received an IP packet of size $3204$ bytes with an IP header of length $20$ bytes. If the values of the datagram length and offset fields of the last IP fragment are $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively, then $\alpha + 3 \beta = $_________

Mark all the context-free languages given below. (Mark all the appropriate choices)

  1. $L = \{x\#w \mid x,w \in \Sigma^* \text{ and } x \text{ is a substring of } w\}$
  2. $L=\{a^nb^{n+m}c^{n+m}d^{n}\mid n,m \geq 0\}$
  3. $L = \{xww_R \mid w \in (a+b)^*,x \in (a+b)^+\}$
  4. $L = \{0^n1^m0^m1^n\mid m,n \geq 0\}$
If an ordinary generating function sequence is $\{a_n\}_{0}^{\infty} = \frac{x}{(1-3x)^2}$. Then $a_4 - a_1$ is equal to _________

A shift reduce parser carries out the actions specified within braces immediately after reducing with the corresponding rule of grammar:

$S \rightarrow S + T \quad \{\text{print ("+")}\}$

$\qquad \mid T \quad \{\;\}$

$T \rightarrow T \ast F \quad \{\text{print ("*")}\}$

$\qquad \mid F \quad \{\;\}$

$F\rightarrow \text{num } \quad \{\text{print (num.val)}\}$

What is the translation of $2 \ast 3 + 7$ using the syntax directed translation scheme described by the above rules?

  1. $237\ast +$
  2. $23 \ast7 +$
  3. $23+7\ast$
  4. $+\ast 237$

The number of view equivalent serial schedules of the given schedule is ________

In a graph, a vertex is called an articulation point if removing it and all the edges associated with it results in the increase of the number of connected components in the graph. Let $G$ be a graph contain $10$ vertices, if $G$ has $8$ articulation points then what must be the number of edges in graph $G$?
  1. $45$
  2. $10$
  3. $9$
  4. $8$
A fair die is thrown as long as necessary for $6$ to turn up. If the number of throws $(n)$ turns out to be odd, the probability that $n=5$ is ______ (rounded to three decimal places)

What is the worst case time complexity in building a heap of $n$ elements?

  1. $\Theta(n\log n)$
  2. $\Theta(n^2)$
  3. $\Theta(n*\log n *\log n)$
  4. $\Theta(n)$

Which of the following is a valid partition of the set $\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$?
  1. $\{1,2\}\{2,3,4\}\{4,5,6\}$
  2. $\{2,4,6\}\{1,3,5\}$
  3. $\{1,4,5\}\{2,6\}$
  4. $\{2\}\{3,6\}\{4,5\}$

For the relation $R(A,B,C,D),$ on which the following functional dependencies hold $F:\{A \rightarrow B,B\rightarrow C, C \rightarrow A\}, G:\{A \rightarrow BC, B \rightarrow A, C \rightarrow A\}.$ Which of the following is correct?(Mark all the appropriate options)

  1. $F$ covers $G$
  2. $G$ covers $F$
  3. $F \equiv G$
  4. $F \not\equiv G$
Consider a selection sorting implementation which takes $8$ time units for input of size $8$. How much time units will it take for an input of size $32?$

Consider the system of equations given below:

  • $2x_1 + 4x_2 + x_3 + 2.6x_4 = 0$
  • $2.6x_1 + 4.6x_2 + 1.6x_3 + 3.2x_4 = 0$
  • $x_1 + 2x_2 + 3x_3 + 3.6x_4 = 0$
  • $3.2x_1 + 5.2x_2 + 2.2x_3 + 3.8x_4 = 0$

The number of independent solutions of the system of equations is?

  1. $1$
  2. $2$
  3. $3$
  4. $4$

What is the output of the following program?

#include<stdio.h>
int main()
{
    int i=0;
    for(i++;i==1;i=2)
    printf("Inside loop ");
    printf("Outside loop");
    return 0;
}
  1. Inside loop Outside loop
  2. Outside loop
  3. Infinite times Inside loop
  4. Syntax error in for loop statement

A hash table is given with $4$ elements. Linear Probing is used for collision avoidance. A biased coin is tossed with the probability of appearance of head being $\dfrac{1}{5}$. An element is added to the table if it is head otherwise one element is removed. What is the chance that after $4$ trials the load factor of the hash table remains same? (Up to three decimal points)

Let in a network the router has been connected in tree topology, such that the structure creates a full binary tree with $16$ routers at leaves. (A full binary tree has all level full). The routers at last but one level to detect the routers at the same level sends ICMP packets to other routers. The minimum possible $TTL$ value is set. What is the expected value of $TTL$ for successful detection?

Consider a FAT file system where disk is divided into $M\;\text{byte}$ blocks, and every FAT entry can store an $N\;\text{bit}$ block number. What is the maximum size of a disk partition that can be managed by such a FAT design?

  1. $2^{M} \ast N \;\text{bytes}$
  2. $2^{N} \ast M \;\text{bytes}$
  3. $2^{N} \ast 2^{M} \;\text{bytes}$
  4. $N \ast M \;\text{bytes}$

Consider the following C program:

#include<stdio.h>
#include<string.h>
int main()
{
    int x = 1;
    char *y;
    y=(char*)&x;
    if(*y == 1)
        printf("%s", "yes");
    else
        printf("%s","no");
    return 0;
}

What will be the output of the above code?

  1. yes
  2. no
  3. Output depends on the system
  4. Undefined behavior
Consider a $B$-tree in which the search key is $16$ bytes long, block size is $4096$ bytes, data pointer is $4$ bytes and block pointer is $8$ bytes. The maximum order of $B$-tree will be ________

Consider the following C function.

int func(int n)
{
    int i, j, k, p, q=1;
    for(i=1 ; i<= n;i=i+1)
    {
        p=0;
        for(k=1 ; k <= n ; k=k+2)
            p++;
        for(j=n ; j>= 1 ; j=j/2)
            q=q*2;
    }
    return q;
}


Which one of the following is the approximate value return by the above function?

  1. $\Theta(n^2)$
  2. $\Theta(n^n)$
  3. $\Theta(2^{n^2})$
  4. $\Theta(2^{n\log \log n)}$

What is time complexity of Dijkstra's algorithm if we use sorted linked list instead of min-heap or priority queue. Assume graph $G(V,E)$ is represented by an adjacency list and $|V| = v$ and $|E| = e.$
  1. $\Theta((v + e)\log v)$
  2. $\Theta(v^2 + e \log v)$
  3. $\Theta(v . e)$
  4. $\Theta(v^2)$

The following circuit implements a two-input $NAND$ gate using two $2\times1$ multiplexers.



What are the values of $X_1,X_2,X_3?$

  1. $X_1=B,X_2=1,X_3=1$
  2. $X_1=A,X_2=0,X_3=A$
  3. $X_1=A,X_2=B,X_3=0$
  4. $X_1=B,X2=0,X_3=A$

Consider the following languages.

  • $L_{1} = \left\{\left\langle M \right\rangle \mid M \text{ takes at least 2021 steps on some input} \right\}$,
  • $L_{2} = \left\{\left\langle M \right\rangle \mid M \text { takes at most 2021 steps on all inputs} \right\}$ and
  • $L_{3} = \left\{\left\langle M \right\rangle \mid M \ \text {accepts every string of length } 21\right\}$,

where for each Turing machine $M,\left\langle M \right\rangle$ denotes a specific encoding of $M$. Which one of the following is/are TRUE? (Mark all the appropriate choices)

  1. $L_{1}$ is recursive and $L_{2}$ and $L_{3}$ are recursively enumerable
  2. $L_{2}$ is recursive and $L_{1}$ and $L_{3}$ are not recursive
  3. $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ are recursive and $L_{3}$ is not recursive
  4. $L_{1}, L_{2}, L_{3}$ are recursively enumerable

In the sequential circuit shown below, if the initial value of the output $Q_0Q_1$ is $01,$ what are the next five values of $Q_0Q_1?$
 

  1. $11,01,10,00,11$
  2. $00,01,00,01,00$
  3. $10,00,11,01,10$
  4. $11,10,01,00,11$

Which of the following formulas is a Correct formalization of the sentence:
$ ext{"There is a book which is not used by any student"}$
Here, $Uses(x,y)$ denotes $x$ uses $y$
  1. $\exists x(Book(x) \ \wedge \ orall y( eg Student(y) \ \wedge eg Uses(y, x)))$
  2. $\exists x(Book(x) ightarrow orall y(Student(y) ightarrow eg Uses(y, x)))$
  3. $\exists x(Book(x) \wedge orall y(Student(y) ightarrow eg Uses(y, x)))$
  4. None of the above

A contractor has to get completed a task of $w$ units. He assigns Mr. $X$ for this work. Further Mr. $X$ divides this work into $3$ people because a person takes responsibility to do the work only if it is a single unit of work, otherwise, he divides the work among $3$ people such that first one performs half of the work and second person performs the one third of the work and the remaining work is being performed by the third person. And, in assigning $w$ units of work to some persons, it costs $w$ rupees. The total expenditure to perform the task will be

  1. $\Theta(\log(w))$
  2. $\Theta(2^{(w)} \log^2(w))$
  3. $\Theta(w\log(w))$
  4. $\Theta(2^{2 \log(w)} \log^2(w))$

Meera, Priya and David are three students that took the Logic exam. Let's consider a propositional language where $p$ represents “Meera passed the exam”, $q$ represents “Priya passed the exam”,and $r$ represents "David passed the exam".
Which of the following is the formal representation of the sentence “Exactly one, among Meera, Priya and David, passed the exam”?
  1. $(p \wedge eg q \wedge eg r )\vee ( eg p \wedge q \wedge eg r)\vee ( eg p \wedge eg q \wedge r)$
  2. $(p \vee eg q \vee eg r )\wedge ( eg p \vee q \vee eg r)\wedge ( eg p \vee eg q \vee r)$
  3. $(p \wedge eg q \wedge eg r )\wedge ( eg p \wedge q \wedge eg r)\wedge ( eg p \wedge eg q \wedge r)$
  4. None of the above

Consider the basic block given below:

p = a + b
q = p - c
p = q * d
p = e - p
q = q + c

The minimum number of nodes and edges present in the DAG representation of the above basic block respectively are ________

  1. $\text{6 and 6}$
  2. $\text{11 and 10}$
  3. $\text{7 and 8}$
  4. $\text{9 and 8}$

What is the output of the following program?

#include<stdio.h>
void fun1(int *x);
void fun2(int *y);
int a;
int main()
{
    a=5;
    fun1(&a);
    printf("%d\n",a);
    return 0;
}
void fun1(int *b)
{
    int a = *b-2;
    fun2(&a);
    *b = a+1;
    printf("%d",a);
}
void fun2(int *c)
{
    *c-=a;
    printf("%d",*c);
}

 

  1. $420$
  2. $-2-2-1$
  3. $-234$
  4. $-2-1-1$

Which of the following is/are correct?(Mark all the appropriate choices)

  1. Post Office Protocol (POP) allows you to read the mail only after downloading it.
  2. In Post Office Protocol (POP), the mail can only be accessed from a single device at a time.
  3. In Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP), the messages can be accessed across multiple devices.
  4. In Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP), the mail content can be read partially before downloading.

Which of the following IP address(es) can be assigned to an Internet interface? (Mark all the appropriate choices)
  1. $10.180.48.224$
  2. $9.255.255.10$
  3. $192.168.20.223$
  4. $172.16.200.18$

Let $R (A, B, C,D,E,G)$ be a relational schema with the following functional dependencies:
$\{AB \rightarrow C, AC \rightarrow B, AD \rightarrow E,B \rightarrow D, BC \rightarrow A, E \rightarrow G,C \rightarrow D,A \rightarrow G,D \rightarrow E\}$ and The decomposition of $R$ into $(A, B, C), (A, B,D,E),(E,G)$

  1. gives a lossless join, and is dependency preserving.
  2. gives a lossless join, but is not dependency preserving.
  3. does not give a lossless join, but is dependency preserving
  4. does not give a lossless join and is not dependency preserving.

A computer system has a $16K$ word cache organized in block-set-associative manner with $4$ blocks per set, $32$ words per block. The number of bits in the SET and WORD fields of the main memory address format is:

  1. $6, 4$
  2. $4, 5$
  3. $5, 5$
  4. $7, 5$

Which of the following statements is/are TRUE? Assume no end markers are available for the input strings. (Mark all the appropriate choices)

  1. The class of language accepted by non-deterministic finite automata and deterministic finite automata are the same.
  2. The class of language accepted by non-deterministic finite push down automata and deterministic finite push down automata are the same.
  3. The class of language accepted by non-deterministic finite push down automata accepting by final state and non-deterministic finite push down automata accepting by empty stack are the same.
  4. The class of language accepted by deterministic finite push down automata accepting by final state and deterministic finite push down automata accepting by empty stack are the same.
